articles.title: Video Friday: An Italian Humanoid Comes to Life
articles.summary: IEEE Spectrum’s robotics roundup highlights multiple Physical AI and robotics developments, including Generative Bionics’ GENE.01 humanoid platform, Generalist’s GEN-1 embodied foundation model for varied robotic hands and tools, and Flexion’s use of Niantic Spatial and Nvidia tools for real-world site scanning and reinforcement-learning policy transfer. The article also notes real-world deployment signals such as Wing drone delivery of urgent NHS pathology samples in South West London and Aurora’s next-generation autonomous freight driver targeting lower hardware cost and longer durability.

articles.title: Generalist’s GEN-1 foundation model now supports a range of robot end effectors
articles.summary: Generalist said its GEN-1 embodied foundation model now supports a broad range of robot end effectors, from five-fingered hands to specialized tools. The model is pretrained on an in-house robotics dataset spanning more than 500,000 hours of real interaction data and about 9,000 end-effector variations, with the goal of learning sensorimotor policies that transfer across different robot forms and tools.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a credible physical AI development showing how robotics models may move beyond single-purpose automation toward more flexible, tool-aware systems. For advisor conversations, the read-through is that robotics adoption could increasingly depend on data scale, model generalization, and hardware-software integration rather than only mechanical design, though the article does not provide customer, revenue, or deployment details.
